claims.text: Periodic, well-bonded interfaces in multilayer HEA coatings block dislocation glide.
Periodic, well-bonded interfaces in multilayer HEA coatings block dislocation climb.
Blocking dislocation glide and climb retards creep relative to a monolithic HEA coating.
The multilayer coating is engineered to contain coherent or semi-coherent interfaces between HEA layers of nearly identical bulk chemistry.
At approximately 600 °C under load, creep in HEAs can involve dislocation-mediated deformation.
At approximately 600 °C under a moderate load, diffusional creep and dislocation climb are activated.
Engineered interfaces act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
Engineered interfaces obstruct diffusion pathways and interrupt continuous plastic flow.
Alternating HEA layers impede dislocation nucleation.
Alternating HEA layers impede dislocation glide and climb.
The interfacial barriers restrict cumulative dislocation movement.
The interfacial barriers limit grain-boundary or interfacial diffusion that would otherwise accelerate creep in monolithic materials.
The multilayer coating will have a lower steady-state creep rate than the monolithic coating.
The multilayer coating will show delayed onset of macroscopic plastic deformation relative to the monolithic coating.
The proposed mechanism applies when dislocation-mediated and diffusion-controlled creep govern deformation.
The proposed benefit depends on interfaces remaining intact without delamination or early cracking.
Layer thickness and interfacial chemistry could modulate the creep-resistance effect.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in steady-state creep rate or cumulative plastic strain in the multilayer sample would falsify the hypothesis.
Observation of no interfacial hindrance to dislocation motion would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The intervention calls the multilayer and monolithic samples identical in microstructure, but one sample necessarily contains engineered coherent or semi-coherent multilayer interfaces while the other is monolithic. The baseline more plausibly requires only similar phase composition and grain size.
